title: Raise default_statistics_target to sharpen GetUserTweets index selectivity
configuration_cause: default_statistics_target=100 leaves histogram/MCV resolution coarse for the skewed tweets.user_id distribution; GetUserTweets (87.9% of terminal capacity, p50 151us, p95 448us) is an Index Scan whose row estimate drives plan choice, and the r002 cache/planner-cost bundle raised TPS but refuted the p95-latency prediction, so the residual bottleneck is estimate quality rather than cache capacity.
mechanism: GetUserTweets dominates terminal occupancy at 87.9% and is served by an Index Scan; its cost depends on the planner's selectivity estimate for the skewed user_id predicate. default_statistics_target=100 caps histogram buckets and MCV list length, so estimates for heavy-hitter users are coarse and the executor may over-read index/heap pages per call. Raising the target to 400 (within [50,500]) quadruples resolution, tightening selectivity estimates and reducing per-call page touches and p50/p95 latency, freeing terminal capacity for higher successful TPS. This is a distinct mechanism class from the refuted cache-capacity bundle: it targets estimate resolution, not buffer size or cost constants.
query_effect: Sharper column statistics for tweets.user_id should let the planner pick a tighter index path for GetUserTweets, reducing pages read per call and lowering its p50/p95 latency; plan_evidence root remains Index Scan.
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful_transaction_tps (>=0.5%) as GetUserTweets terminal occupancy falls.
expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50 and p95 decrease; overall p95 flat-to-slightly-down.

predictions.rationale: Higher stats resolution tightens selectivity for skewed user_id, reducing pages touched per GetUserTweets call.
Lower GetUserTweets terminal occupancy frees finite client terminal capacity for more completed transactions.
Better estimates reduce worst-case over-reads on heavy-hitter users, trimming the p95 tail.

alternatives.statement: If the residual bottleneck is buffer capacity rather than estimate resolution, raising shared_buffers further (already 65536) would lower GetUserTweets latency; but r002 already tested cache capacity and refuted the p95 prediction, so this is less likely.

If GetUserTweets latency is dominated by WAL sync queueing (wal_wait anomaly, sync_average_ms 0.14), the WAL commit-path bundle would lower InsertTweet latency and raise TPS without changing GetUserTweets p50.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Targets a mechanism class (estimate resolution) not yet tested, distinct from the refuted cache-capacity bundle; a bounded statistics-target increase is low-risk and can only tighten estimates, with a clear falsifiable p50 prediction.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Quadruple from 100 to 400 within safe [50,500]; 4x resolution for skewed user_id histograms while keeping ANALYZE cost bounded.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: column statistics resolution for skewed predicate selectivity

nodes.label: Finer selectivity estimates for skewed user_id reduce GetUserTweets pages per call

cross_domain_requirements: ANALYZE must run after the reload for new statistics to take effect; executor should trigger ANALYZE on tweets.
